items.title: OBJECT DETECTION IN WIRELESS CHARGING
items.abstract: The present disclosure relates to methods and systems that can reliably detect foreign objects on a wireless charging pad under varying temperatures. In some examples, an object detector can utilize a set of inductive coils included in resonant tanks, and excite the resonant tanks using signals in a range of frequencies including or near a nominal resonant frequency of the resonant tanks. The object detector can detect a metal object based on resistance of a coil increasing and inductance of the coil decreasing. By analyzing the shifts and/or distributions in resonant frequencies and output magnitudes (e.g., output voltage peaks), the object detector can distinguish between changes of frequencies and magnitudes caused by temperature and those caused by foreign objects to accurately detect the foreign objects.

A wireless charging system comprising: a resonant tank comprising a coil; an exciter electrically connected to the resonant tank; and a processing circuit in communication with at least the exciter, the processing circuit configured to: cause the exciter to excite the resonant tank; determine a first parameter indicative of inductance of the coil and a second parameter indicative of resistance of the coil associated with the coil being excited; and detect an object based on the first parameter indicating a decrease in inductance and the second parameter indicating an increase in resistance relative to when the object is not present, wherein the object may be a metal object.
claims.2: 2. The wireless charging system of Claim 1, wherein the first parameter comprises a resonant frequency of the resonant tank and the second parameter comprises a magnitude of an output voltage of the resonant tank.
claims.3: 3. The wireless charging system of Claim 1 or 2, wherein the processing circuit is configured to excite the resonant tank by at least sequentially applying a first plurality of signals to the resonant tank, each of the first plurality of signals generated based on a frequency of a plurality of frequencies, and wherein the processing circuit is configured to determine the first parameter and the second parameter by at least: measuring an output magnitude at an output terminal of the resonant tank associated with each of the first plurality of signals being applied to the resonant tank to obtain a first plurality of output magnitudes; and selecting one of the plurality of frequencies corresponding to a first maximum output magnitude among the first plurality of output magnitudes as a first resonant frequency of the resonant tank, wherein the first parameter comprises the first resonant frequency and the second parameter comprises the first maximum output magnitude.

items.title: WIRELESS CHARGING SYSTEM AND WIRELESS POWER TRANSMITTING DEVICE
items.abstract: A wireless power transmitting device comprises a first coil structure and a control circuit. The first coil structure comprises a first circuit board and a plurality of turns of a coil conductor arranged on the first circuit board. The coil conductor comprises at least one first capacitor structure. Linear distance between the first capacitor structure and an output terminal of the coil conductor is shorter than the linear distance between the first capacitor structure and an input terminal of the coil conductor. Position of the first capacitor structure does not overlap with position of the output terminal. The control circuit measures the first coil structure to determine a power transfer value and determine whether a foreign object has entered a power transmission range between the wireless power transmitting device and the receiving device according to the power transfer value.

items.title: AN APPARATUS
items.abstract: An apparatus comprising a power-emitting device comprising an antenna, power circuitry configured to provide power via the antenna for wireless charging of a power-receiving device, and a processor, the processor configured to at least analyse signals from said antenna to determine the presence of the power-receiving device proximal the power-emitting device and to determine the presence of a foreign object, FO, proximal the power-emitting device. Wherein the processor is configured to control the power circuitry to either interrupt or not initiate said provision of power for wireless charging of the power-receiving device based on said analysis of on one or both of said analysis of the signals and the power provided by the power circuitry being indicative of the power-emitting device being proximal to a foreign object. In response to said analysis of the signals being indicative that a FO-removal event has occurred, the processor is configured to control the power circuitry to provide power for wireless charging of the power-receiving device.

claims.1: 1. items.title: WIRELESS CHARGING FOREIGN OBJECT DETECTION
items.abstract: A method (300) of foreign object detection for a wireless power transmitter (100, 600). The method (300) includes determining a vector impedance of a near-field communication (NFC) coil (102, 602) with an NFC chip (108, 608). The determined vector impedance includes an impedance amplitude component and an impedance phase component. The impedance amplitude component and the impedance phase component are compared to a baseline impedance amplitude and a baseline impedance phase. A determination as to whether an object is present within an inductive charging area of the wireless power transmitter (100, 600) is made when a difference between the determined vector impedance, and the baseline impedance amplitude and the baseline impedance phase, exceeds a delta threshold. A ping signal is generated with a charging source coil (104, 604) when the object is determined to be present. A foreign object is detected based on whether a response signal to the ping signal is received from the object.

items.abstract: A method of performing thermal management of an energy storage device (240; 702) includes providing an energy storage device (240; 702) selectively connectable to an air conditioning system and including a plurality of individual cells (702a-702e). The method includes evaluating a temperature of the plurality of individual cells (702a-702e) to determine a most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device (240; 702), comparing the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device (240; 702) to a desired operating temperature range of the energy storage device (240; 702), and adjusting one or more parameters associated with the energy storage device (240; 702) in response to determining that the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device (240; 702) is outside of the desired operating temperature range.

claims.1: 1. A method of performing thermal management of an energy storage device (240; 702), the method comprising: providing the energy storage device, the energy storage device being selectively connectable to an air conditioning system and including a plurality of individual cells (702a-702e); evaluating a temperature of the plurality of individual cells to determine a most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device; comparing the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device to a desired operating temperature range of the energy storage device; and adjusting one or more parameters associated with the energy storage device in response to determining that the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device is outside of the desired operating temperature range.
claims.2: 2. The method of claim 1, further comprising identifying a plurality of temperatures across the energy storage device.
claims.3: 3. The method of claim 2, wherein identifying the plurality of temperatures across the energy storage device includes sensing each of the plurality of temperatures at a respective cell of the plurality of individual cells via a temperature sensor (T1-T5).
claims.4: 4. The method of claim 2, wherein identifying the plurality of temperatures across the energy storage device includes: sensing at least a portion of the plurality of temperatures via a plurality of temperature sensors (T1-T5) spaced about the energy storage device, wherein the plurality of temperature sensors is less than the plurality of individual cells; and estimating the temperature at at least one of the plurality of individual cells.
claims.5: 5. The method of any of claims 3-4, wherein evaluating the temperature of the plurality of individual cells to determine a most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device includes determining a maximum temperature of the energy storage device, a minimum temperature of the energy storage device, an average cell temperature of the energy storage device and a temperature profile at each of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device in response to the plurality of temperatures associated with each of the plurality of individual cells.
claims.6: 6. The method of any of claims 1-5, wherein adjusting one or more parameters associated with the energy storage device in response to determining that the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device is outside of the desired operating temperature range includes cooling the energy storage device, optionally wherein the energy storage device is cooled when the average cell temperature is greater than a first warm threshold.
claims.7: 7. The method of any of claims 1-6, wherein adjusting one or more parameters associated with the energy storage device in response to determining that the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device is outside of the desired operating temperature range includes shutting down one or more of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device having a temperature outside of the desired operating range, optionally wherein one or more of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device are shut down when the most relevant temperature parameter is greater than a second warm threshold.
claims.8: 8. The method of any of claims 1-7, wherein adjusting one or more parameters associated with the energy storage device in response to determining that the most relevant temperature parameter of the energy storage device is outside of the desired operating temperature range includes heating the energy storage device.
claims.9: 9. claims.10: 10. The method of any of claims 1-9, further comprising approximating the remaining life of each of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device.
claims.11: 11. The method of claim 10, wherein adjusting one or more parameters associated with the energy storage device in response to determining that the at least one of the plurality of individual cells has a temperature outside of the desired operating temperature range is performed to maximize the remaining life of the energy storage device.
claims.12: 12. The method of claim 10, wherein approximating the remaining life of each of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device further includes tracking a total time that each of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device is at a respective temperature, optionally wherein approximating the remaining life of each of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device further includes determining an accumulated age of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device based on the total time that each of the plurality of individual cells of the energy storage device is at the respective temperature.
claims.13: 13. The method of any of claims 10-12, further comprising determining if one or more of the plurality of individual cells is compromised based on the remaining life.
claims.14: 14. items.abstract: An air conditioning system (700) includes a vapor compression loop (704) including a compressor (710), an expansion device (714), a first heat exchanger (712), and a second heat exchanger (716). A working fluid (R) is configured to circulate within the vapor compression loop (704). An electric energy storage device (702) is selectively operable to supply power to a component of the air conditioning system (700). A thermal management system (730) is associated with the electric energy storage device (702). The thermal management system (730) includes a first heat transfer component (740) and a second heat transfer component (742). The first heat transfer component (740) is thermally coupled to the vapor compression loop (704) during cooling of the electric energy storage device (702) and the second heat transfer component (742) is thermally coupled to the vapor compression loop (704) during heating of the electric energy storage device (702).

items.abstract: The present invention relates to an electrode device.In order to provide an improved thermal management of a battery system, the electrode device (10), comprises a support structure (12), an electroactive structure (14) and a heat transfer structure (16). The support structure is configured for carrying the electroactive structure and the heat transfer structure. The electroactive structure is configured for storing and releasing of charge carriers (18). The heat conductivity of the heat transfer structure is higher than the heat conductivity of any of the support structure or the electroactive structure. The electroactive structure is arranged at the support structure. The heat transfer structure is arranged at the electroactive structure. The heat transfer structure is oriented to guide heat (20) away from a surface (22) of the electroactive structure to prevent thermal tensions (24) in its vicinity while providing diffusivity of the charge carriers to the surface

items.abstract: An electric battery group (1) comprises a plurality of battery cells (4) within a container (2), spaced apart from each other by spacer frames (6) such as to define spaces (8) between the cells (4). The battery cells (4) are configured and arranged to come into direct contact with a flow of a temperature-regulating liquid that passes through the spaces (8) between the cells (4) for maintaining the battery cells (4) within a determined temperature field. Each spacer frame (6) is a peripheral frame having an upper crossbeam (6A), a lower crossbeam (6B) and two vertical columns (6C) connecting the upper crossbeam (6A) to the lower crossbeam (6B). The upper crossbeam (6A) has opposite ends connected to the vertical columns (6C) via respective restricted sections (18) acting as hinges. In the event that, following a thermal runaway of one or more cells, the outlet manifold (14) fills with pressurized gas, the pressure of the gases causes a rotation of the upper crossbeam (6A), from a position in which a communication space is defined between the upper crossbeam (6A) and an adjacent cell (4), to a position in which said communication space is interrupted, so that the gases present in the outlet manifold (14) cannot flow into the spaces (8) between the cells (4) in the direction of the inlet manifold (12).

items.abstract: Two-phase immersion cooling systems for electronics are disclosed herein. In some embodiments, a device includes a base having a first side and a second side, and a plurality of blades each coupled to and extending from the second side of the base along an axis substantially normal to an outer surface of the second side. Individual ones of the blades (i) include first through fourth sides, (ii) are spaced apart from one another such that fluid can flow therebetween, and (iii) include a plurality of microfeatures at the third and/or fourth sides of the respective blade. The microfeatures increase an exposed surface area of the respective blade and adjacent microfeatures define microchannels therebetween. Individual ones of the microchannels extend along the axis and have a width between 1 femtometer and 1 millimeter. The base and the blades are configured to be submerged in a cooling fluid.

items.title: COMPOUND FOR A TWO-PHASE IMMERSION COOLANT
items.abstract: Disclosed herein is the compound CCC=C(F)CF. The compound can be provided as a pure isomer of either the E-isomer or Z-isomer, or as a diastereomeric mixture of both isomers (i.e., an E/Z mixture). The boiling point and dielectric constant of the compound enable effective use of the compound as a coolant in a two-phase immersion cooling system. A two-phase immersion cooling system incorporating the compound as coolant can include: an immersion tank configured to contain the coolant and to contain a component capable of generating heat; and a condenser configured to receive vaporized coolant and to condense the vaporized coolant back to liquid form.
